full_judgment:
A Division Bench issued rule nisi calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed to restore the vacant possession of the buildings and houses, place of business and residence at Kandupatti (situated at the central point of Malitola-Nawabpur-English Road in Dhaka) to the several hundred sex workers who had been evicted therefrom on May 11 and 12, 1997 in the manner not authorised by law and why they should not be directed to set the law into motion against the persons who took law in their own hands in evicting the inmates of the Kandupatti and why they should not be directed to provide to the sex workers full security at Kandupatti so that they may enjoy their fundamental rights as guaranteed under Articles 31, 40 and 43 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 In the petition it is stated that six hundred sex workers were evicted from their place of residence and occupation by unruly mobs Ied by the Local Ward Commissioner, Hossain Mollah on May 11 and 12, 1997 "under the very nose of the law enforcing agency. News of such eviction was published in the daily newspapers on 13 May, 1997. The news as published "witnesses and police sources said the mob was led by local Ward Commissioner, Hossain Mollah, said to be the owner of one of the buildings of the brothel. The local people wanted to evict the brothel obviously for social reason and religious sentiments, but about 40 years old Mollah has a cross purpose." She further states that an en-masse eviction is clear violation of fundamental rights of the sex workers and in the wake of eviction they sought police help in vain. Their properties and ornaments and money were looted by the goondas. The law enforcing agency did not take any step to save them from such helpless situation. This eviction continued for two days. The petitioners annexed the newspaper cutting to this writ petition. The petition was resisted by affidavit-in-opposition filed by respondent No. 5, the Officer-in-Charge of Kotwali Police Station, Dhaka. It states that actual facts were suppressed in the writ petition. According to him, some Sardarnis of the sex workers viz. Manu alias Rahima, Manju and Renu and some other sarders viz. Nurul Islam and Shukur used to collect some girls from various places and used to do the sex business through them through amicable agreement of the house owners. Due to social pressure of the local residence, Musullies of the two mosques, teachers and students of Azizia Islamia Boys’ and Girls'' School, Kaji Mazharul Haque Boys'' and Girls'' Primary School, the Manager Law College, the employees and officers of DESA situated nearby to the brothel raised objection against such activities of the owners but they were reluctant to evict from their respective houses the said sex workers who were in number about 50 or 60 and the statement of evicted six hundred sex workers was false. The allegation of inaction of the local Commissioner of the Ward and the police was denied. It further states that Mrs. Salma Ali, Executive Director, Mohila Ain Zibi Samity with her associates visited the area and recovered three minor girls and started police case No. 20 dated 7-5-97 with Kotwali Police Station that was followed in respect of three sardarnis, Banu alias Rahima, Manju and Parul and one sarder Nurul Islam, It is also stated that on investigation it was found that alleged sex workers have no licence. However, subsequently, inquiry was held and police recovered thirty minor girls. Some of them were sent to Mirpur Vagabond Centre. In affidavit-in-reply the statement made by respondent No. 5 that there were 50/60 sex workers in Kandupatti is denied by the petitioner in her affidavit-in-reply and it is asserted that there were about six hundred sex workers at Kandupatti. Further, it denied that they did voluntarily leave the place. In paragraph 5 of the affidavit-in-reply the petitioner stated the names of above 120 sex workers and it includes sex workers'' affidavit sworn on different dates spreading over 60 to 118. It also denied the statement made in paragraph 14 of the affidavit-in-opposition stating that it was not correct to say that the matter is disputed in between the sex workers and private house owners and the government cannot restore the possession of the sex workers to their place of business. It was further stated that subsequent written complaint by the sex workers on 4-6-97 under registered cover was not given any importance and no action was taken upon that by the officer-in-charge who suppressed this fact in the statement made in affidavit-in-opposition with ulterior motive and malafide.
